blocks.prompt: 11. If Salman starts with Rs. 5,000 and saves Rs. 1,000 monthly, derive \(S(n)\) and prove it by induction.
blocks.explanation:
A real-life question in two parts: first derive \(S(n)\), the savings after \(n\) months, then prove it by induction.
He starts with Rs. 5,000 and adds Rs. 1,000 at the end of every month.
Plan: table, pattern \(S(n) = 5000 + 1000n\), rule \(S(k + 1) = S(k) + 1000\), induction.
steps:
Given: starting amount Rs. 5,000; Rs. 1,000 saved every month.
To find: \(S(n)\), the total savings after \(n\) months, and a proof by induction.
Method: Spot the pattern from a few months, then mathematical induction.

Make a table and spot the pattern
\[S(1) = 6000,\ S(2) = 7000,\ S(3) = 8000\]
\[S(n) = 5000 + 1000n\]
Why: After \(n\) months he has added Rs. 1,000 exactly \(n\) times to the starting Rs. 5,000.

Statement and monthly rule
\[P(n): S(n) = 5000 + 1000n\]
\[S(k + 1) = S(k) + 1000\]
Why: Each month adds Rs. 1,000. We call the statement \(P(n)\) because \(S(n)\) is already the name of the savings.

Base case: \(n = 1\)
\[S(1) = 5000 + 1000 = 6000\]
\[5000 + 1000(1) = 6000\]
So \(P(1)\) is true.
Why: After one month he has his Rs. 5,000 plus one saving of Rs. 1,000.

Induction hypothesis: assume \(P(k)\)
\[S(k) = 5000 + 1000k \quad (A)\]
Why: We suppose the formula is right after \(k\) months.

Inductive step: use the rule, then (A)
\[S(k + 1) = S(k) + 1000\]
\[= 5000 + 1000k + 1000\]
\[= 5000 + 1000(k + 1)\]
So \(P(k + 1)\) is true.
Why: (A) replaces \(S(k)\); \(1000k + 1000 = 1000(k + 1)\). This is the formula with \(n = k + 1\).

Conclusion
\(P(1)\) is true and \(P(k) \Rightarrow P(k + 1)\). By the principle of mathematical induction, \(S(n) = 5000 + 1000n\) for every positive integer \(n\).
Why: Both conditions of the principle hold.

Check: \(n = 12\) (one year)
\[S(12) = 5000 + 12{,}000 = 17{,}000\]
Why: 12 savings of Rs. 1,000 added to Rs. 5,000 give Rs. 17,000.
blocks.final_answer: \(S(n) = 5000 + 1000n\) rupees after \(n\) months, proved by induction.
